Building Condition Survey — Westbridge University, Hollis Building
Survey date: 14 March. Surveyor: J. Whitfield, Estates Compliance Office.
Scope. The survey covered all four floors of the Hollis Building, the basement plant room, the service corridor linking the building to the car park, and the external loading bay. Occupancy at the time of the visit was approximately one hundred and twenty staff and postgraduate students. The building is a reinforced concrete frame with brick cladding, constructed in 1968 and refurbished in 2007.
Envelope. Cladding panels on the north elevation showed minor hairline cracking around two window openings on the third floor. No water ingress was recorded at the time of the visit, but the seals should be renewed within the next financial year. The flat roof membrane was replaced in 2019 and remains under warranty until 2029. Two rainwater outlets were obstructed by leaf litter and were cleared by the maintenance team.
Mechanical and electrical. The gas-fired boilers in the basement plant room passed their annual service with no defects recorded. The building management system reported no outstanding faults, although the third-floor temperature sensor reads approximately two degrees above the calibrated reference and will be replaced. The lift was inspected under the statutory scheme and the certificate is displayed in the lobby. Emergency lighting and fire alarm testing are covered by separate reports held by the compliance office. No asbestos-containing materials were identified in the areas surveyed, and the register held by the estates office matches the observed condition.
Accessibility. The main entrance ramp meets the required gradient and the handrails are secure. The accessible toilet on the ground floor is working and the alarm pull cord was tested. Wayfinding signage is adequate, although the map at the north entrance is out of date and should be reissued. The reception desk is staffed between eight and six on weekdays and the security team keeps a signing-in record for contractors.
Space utilisation. The open-plan office on the second floor is operating at roughly eighty per cent of its designed capacity. Two meeting rooms on the first floor are booked infrequently and could be consolidated. Storage pressure in the basement is significant and the archive store is close to capacity.
The chapel on the third floor. The chapel was included in the survey at the request of the chaplaincy, which occupies the adjoining rooms. The plaster ceiling shows evidence of historic water damage above the west window, although the area is currently dry. The ventilation is inadequate for the number of people who attend services, and the surveyor recommends a small extract fan be installed before next winter. The stone floor at the threshold of the entrance is uneven and presents a minor trip hazard; a temporary mat has been placed and a permanent repair has been added to the maintenance schedule.
Actions. The estates office will raise works orders for the window seals, the temperature sensor and the threshold repair, and will review the signage and storage issues at the next quarterly meeting.
